newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BERLIN - Ad agencies based in Germany -- Europe's biggest advertising market -- have little chance of playing a key role in the international market, says Michael Maedel, European chief executive of J. Walter Thompson. They missed their opportunity when they had it 20 or 30 years ago, he says, and now the concentration of agencies in the industry has progressed too far for them to find a real niche.
CHICAGO - Outdoor Systems Inc. agrees to buy National Advertising Co for $1.0 billion from 3M, the companies say, strengthening its position as the largest U.S. billboard advertising company.

KRONBERG, Germany - Advertising sales house IP Network posted six billion marks ($3.5 billion) in turnover worldwide in 1996, a 4.7 percent increase on the previous year, its German unit says. The German IP unit also saw growth in television ad bookings.
NEW YORK - Interpublic Group of Cos Inc says it has acquired a "significant minority interest" in Nicholson NY, a new media firm.
CHICAGO - Omnicom Group's DDB Needham International, Paris names Kip Keesey president of DDB Central Europe effective June 1.
BREMEN, Germany - Deutsche Telekom AG, the telecoms group, signs sponsoring contract with German Soccer Federation.

NEW YORK - Avon Products Inc agrees to market Mattel's Barbie dolls and other products in the U.S. and a new line of Barbie cosmetics worldwide, in expanded alliance expected to boost Avon's net sales by $100 million annually.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

GENEVA - A bloc of global and national companies and cyberspace bodies, brushing aside reservations from the U.S. and the European Union, have set up a new structure for registering addresses on the Internet. The accord is aimed at ending confusion over allocation of "top-level domain" names, counterparts of telephone numbers on the rapidly expanding Internet which is now used by an estimated 50 million people.

COLOGNE - Germany's number one private television channel RTL says it boosted market share in April while private station Sat1 dropped to third place behind public broadcaster ARD from second place. RTL says its market share rose to 17.8 percent in April from 16.4 percent in the previous month.

NEW YORK - News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch vows to continue with plans to launch a satellite-television service, despite recent suggestions a $1.0 billion deal with EchoStar Communications was unravelling, the Wall Street Journal says.
PARIS - French online information service company Infonie, faced with slower-than-expected growth in subscriber numbers, says it plan capital increase and link-up with another company.

WASHINGTON - Bloomberg LP founder Michael Bloomberg says his financial news and information company is not interested in buying the Dow Jones Markets, formerly called Telerate and a division of Bloomberg's rival, Dow Jones & Co.

FRANKFURT - Catholic and Protestant churches in Germany issue joint warning against concentration of media power in the hands of a few and urge greater controls on the Internet. Church leaders have advised business executives and politicians against allowing profit motives and technology alone to drive developments, criticising an increase in the portrayal of sex and violence on television and on computer networks.
PARIS - French multimedia company IDP seeks listing on the Paris Nouveau Marche start-up market with an Initial Public Offering for 23 to 29 percent of its capital.

CANBERRA - Australian Treasurer Peter Costello rules that CanWest Global Communication Corp's increased economic interest in Ten Group Ltd was inconsistent with foreign investment policy. Costello says Canwest must sell its current 76 percent economic interest down to the previously sanctioned 57.5 percent.
KARLSRUHE, Germany - Newsmagazine "Der Spiegel" posts the biggest turnover among German magazines, business trade publication Kress Report says.
PARIS - A pricing row is delaying French cable television firms from offering Internet access on their networks, the companies involved say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MIAMI - RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp says it and other major U.S. tobacco companies have filed a notice of intent to appeal a North Carolina judge's ruling that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has jurisdiction to regulate tobacco as a drug.

NEW YORK - Eastman Kodak Co says it will sustain its digital imaging growth with new products it is introducing this year and will continue to invest in emerging markets. Kodak President Dan Carp says the company expects its percentage of revenues from outside the U.S. to amount to 75 percent by the year 2001, up from a little over 50 percent now.
RASATT, Germany - Mercedes-Benz AG says its new A-class compact car will hit showrooms in October priced at 30,360 marks for the basic 1.4-litre, 82-horsepower "Classic" version

LONDON - Unilever NV/Plc, the Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group, reports a seven-percent rise in first-quarter profits to 538 million pounds ($873.2 million) pounds, in a low key statement reflecting a weak trading environment. The company says sales in Europe were slightly ahead and profits rose sharply, but profits in North America fell by 11 percent.

CHICAGO - MasterCard International President Jerry McElhatton warns the U.S. banking industry that its role in financial services is being threatened by newcomers riding the new technology wave. "I believe that the financial services business is facing a fundamental upheaval in both structure and delivery," says McElhatton.

PARIS - The head of Andersen Worldwide says he is confident partners of the accountancy and consulting empire would be able to settle their differences after their massive vote in favour of staying together.
The 2,500 partners attending the group's annual meeting in Paris voted by 93 percent to keep Andersen Consulting and Arthur Andersen under one roof.
DARMSTADT, Germany - German cosmetics group Wella AG and Italian luxury goods company Gucci N.V. have agreed to expand their cooperation on Gucci perfume promotion, Wella says.

JOHANNESBURG - Rebounding chicken prices and stable second half costs are expected to help pare Rainbow Chicken Ltd's full year loss by about a third, analysts say. Analysts on average forecast a contraction in Rainbow's pre-exceptional losses to 27.8 cents a share from 43.4 cents a share a year ago.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - Sales growth of personal computers in Europe lost momentum in the first quarter of 1997, held back by stagnant conditions in France and a lacklustre reception for the latest Intel Pentium MMX technology, a new survey says. Outlook for the whole year is uncertain, according to market researcher CONTEXT.

ATLANTIC CITY, New Jersey - The Atlantic City gambling market has a strong growth potential, but must make major improvements to lure new customers amid tough competition and industry consolidation, analysts and company leaders say.

TRANG, Thailand - The crowd surrounding the muddy bullring yells with excitement as drum beats signal the start of the bullfight. It's a far cry from the bullrings of Madrid or Pamplona. In Thailand, bullfighting aficionados come for the gambling, not the sport. In Thailand, matadors do not even exist. It's bull against bull and money is king.
